findings.text: the docstring's second clause, `every case fingerprints the real user-scope settings file before and after`, is unqualified, and test_install_help_lists_the_command (:96) neither names a temporary target nor calls _fingerprint, so the sentence is false for that case; the delivered fragment repeats it verbatim (docs/evidence/fragments/an-orchestrator-cannot-forget-its-obligations/hooks-install-is-a-command.html:52). The previous head's review flagged exactly this overclaim and the repair qualified only the first clause (`Every case that installs ...`), so both artifacts still read as coverage the file does not provide; no risk follows, since --help opens no file, but a reader checking coverage against that sentence is checking a weaker thing than it says.

item_verdicts.diff: read commit by commit against the base; 34df161cb adds the hooks group and the test file, and a750a7992 replaces the inert --scope option with a scopes dict that resolves via install.user_settings_path(), prints the resolved checkout to stderr, restores the reference's instruction to run the command from the main checkout, and makes the test file's guard honest by fingerprinting through the password database while asserting the HOME-redirected default separately.
item_verdicts.done_when: the done-when is the CLI verb wrapping the installer's dry-run/printer contract; tests/test_hooks_install_cli.py holds seven cases over exactly those behaviours (:105 dry run byte-identical, :123 script paths under the checkout and stderr naming it, :155 merge, :174 duplicate refusal, :190 unparsable target, :204 HOME redirect), all seven green in the head arm I re-ran, against 84 passed at the base arm over the four pre-existing files.
item_verdicts.goal: the goal is `reckon hooks install --scope user` prints the coordinator hook settings fragment and merges it only under --write; driven directly at the head through the click runner, the dry run prints the fragment to stdout and leaves the named target byte-identical, --write merges while keeping the target's own keys and hook group, a second --write refuses non-zero, and an unmapped scope on the command's own resolver raises UsageError (reckon/cli.py:6701-6703), so the flag is the resolver rather than an advertisement.
item_verdicts.manifest: read against the tree; its four changed_paths match the commits, its measure figures match both gate logs and my own re-runs, its fingerprint of the real user-scope settings file (mtime 1790606544, size 5997) is what I measured before and after my runs, and its negative-control log's first line repeats the declared mutation verbatim with EXIT=1 last; it names its arms under tests/test_logs rather than baseline_suite/after_suite.
item_verdicts.write_paths: the node's grant is cli.py, the new test file, the harness reference, the plan fragment and an unused figures dir; `git show --name-only` lists exactly four paths for each of 34df161cb and a750a7992 — docs/evidence/fragments/an-orchestrator-cannot-forget-its-obligations/hooks-install-is-a-command.html, reckon/cli.py, skills/reckon-build/references/orchestrator-harness/claude-code.md, tests/test_hooks_install_cli.py — and nothing else, with no plan edit and no terminal status.

justifications.durability: the negative control reds the dry-run byte-identical case and the HOME case under the mutation it declares (I ran it: 2 failed, 5 passed), the real-file guard now resolves through the password database while the default path's HOME-following is asserted by a separate case, and the script-path case derives the checkout from the test file's own location rather than from the installer's helper; deducted because the unmapped-scope UsageError branch cannot be reached through the CLI (one Choice member) and so carries no test, and the guard and the command still resolve their target by different means.
justifications.evidence: I reproduced both arms myself in fresh trees to the same counts and the same two pytest ids, re-ran the declared mutation and saw the named dry-run case go red, drove the command's five stated behaviours rather than inferring them, and confirmed the real settings file is untouched by fingerprint; deducted for the surviving overclaim in the delivered evidence fragment (finding 1), which is the one artifact whose job is to state coverage exactly.
justifications.fit: the command wraps install_hook_settings instead of reimplementing the merge, keeps the module's lazy-import idiom, translates HookInstallError into the click idiom and reuses build_hook_snippet in the tests; deducted because the CLI re-derives the checkout root at reckon/cli.py:6707 as Path(installer.__file__).resolve().parents[2] while the installer derives the same root in interpreter_path(), with nothing pinning the two together, and because the refusal message is composed at the CLI from result.skipped.
justifications.goal_fidelity: the command is the surface the goal names and every behaviour it states was driven directly and held; the refusal's granularity (whole fragment, not any single entry) follows the plan's own revision note, which retires the pre-revision whole-install refusal and which I confirmed against commit 989f93396 in reckon/hooks/install.py, so the node's spec note for adjudication is accurate rather than a mis-citation.
justifications.scope_discipline: four changed paths, all inside the grant; the figures directory in the grant was correctly left unused because the done-when names no figure; the reference and fragment edits are the two artifacts the previous head's review asked for and are in scope; no plan state, index or peer path touched, and the reviewed worktree is clean at the head I read.
